decoded_frames.caption: What if a demo video was not a recording you capture, but a value you compile? This is DemoCreate.
A demo is a declarative spine: scenes of narration chunks, each an ordered stream of typed actions. Three ideas carry the whole system.
Clip duration is measured. Word timing is estimated: the default transcriber spreads known text across the clip by character length. It does not detect spoken word onsets.
YAML configuration selects themes, layout, resolution presets including four K, and encoding controls. Actual quality depends on input detail and encoding settings.
Eight subsystems share a declarative spine. Narration, rendering and export also depend on configuration, assets and the selected runtime environment.
Declarative. Deterministic. Dogfooded. This entire video was compiled by DemoCreate from one file. Edit it, re-render, and never record a take again.
